parameters.content:
## Validate e-invoices from Gmail and book them as Xero draft bills

**Who it's for:** bookkeepers and finance teams in the EU who now receive structured e-invoices (XRechnung, Peppol BIS, ZUGFeRD / Factur-X) by email, and whose accounting tool cannot read them.

### How it works
1. A new unread email with an XML or PDF attachment arrives. It is marked read when the run finishes.
2. **Read The E-Invoice** pulls the invoice data out of the XML, or out of the PDF it is embedded in.
3. Set and If nodes check the key EN 16931 rules: number, dates, parties, VAT id, VAT on every line, and that the sums add up.
4. Broken invoices go back to the supplier naming the rule. Credit notes, other currencies and plain PDFs go to a person.
5. Valid ones become Xero **draft** bills, supplier added if new, duplicates skipped, XML attached, totals compared.

### Setup
1. Connect Gmail and Xero.
2. Fill **E-Invoice Policy**: bookkeeper email, expense account code, base currency.
3. Make sure Xero has your purchase tax rates (e.g. 19% and 7%).

### Use another accounting tool
Sections 1-3 do not know Xero. Swap sections 4-6: replace the Xero calls with HTTP Request nodes for lexoffice, sevDesk or QuickBooks, and map the fields of **Prepare The Xero Bill**.

Bills stay drafts. Nothing is approved or paid.

## 1. Read the invoice
The one Code node: no built-in node reads the XML inside a ZUGFeRD / Factur-X PDF. Everything after it is Set, If and Switch.

## 2. Check the EN 16931 rules
One Set field per rule. To add a rule, add a field whose name starts with check_.

## 3. Answer the supplier or a person
Broken invoices go back to the supplier with the rule. Anything that needs judgement goes to the bookkeeper.

## 4. Match Xero
Which organisation, and which Xero tax type fits each VAT rate. Another tool? Replace these calls, keep the bill fields.

## 5. Book one at a time
Find or add the supplier, and never book the same bill twice.

## 6. Draft, attach, compare
The XML must attach and Xero's totals must match, or the bookkeeper hears why.
